<h1 id="Primal-Composition-Patterns-%E2%80%94-wetSpring">Primal Composition Patterns — wetSpring<a class="anchor-link" href="#Primal-Composition-Patterns-%E2%80%94-wetSpring">¶</a></h1><p>wetSpring is the first spring to implement <strong>pure primal composition</strong> with
zero sovereign HTTP fallbacks. This notebook documents the patterns that
emerged: three-tier fetch routing, structured gap reports, provenance
session lifecycle, and capability wire names. These patterns are the
template for all future springs.</p>
<p><strong>Data sources</strong>: <code>experiments/results/primal_composition.json</code></p>
<p><strong>Reproduce</strong>: <code>cargo run --bin validate_gonzales_provenance_chain</code> in wetSpring.</p>
<hr/>
<p><em>For other springs: this notebook is the reference for how to integrate
with the primal ecosystem. Copy the fetch routing, gap report, and
provenance patterns. When you find new friction, add it to wateringHole.</em></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<h2 id="Three-Tier-Fetch-Routing">Three-Tier Fetch Routing<a class="anchor-link" href="#Three-Tier-Fetch-Routing">¶</a></h2><p>External data (ChEMBL, PubChem) routes through a strict three-tier
hierarchy. Springs never make direct HTTP calls — NestGate handles TLS.
If primals are unavailable, a structured gap report is returned instead
of a fallback.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<h2 id="Provenance-Session-Lifecycle">Provenance Session Lifecycle<a class="anchor-link" href="#Provenance-Session-Lifecycle">¶</a></h2><p>Every data and compute operation in wetSpring is wrapped in a provenance
session: <code>session.create</code> → <code>event.append</code> (N times) → <code>session.commit</code>
→ <code>braid.create</code>. The wire names follow the canonical <code>{DOMAIN}.{OPERATION}</code>
pattern established by primalSpring V082.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<h2 id="Gap-Report-Structure">Gap Report Structure<a class="anchor-link" href="#Gap-Report-Structure">¶</a></h2><p>When a required primal is unavailable, wetSpring returns a structured
JSON gap report instead of falling back to sovereign HTTP or disk.
This surfaces missing capabilities cleanly for primalSpring handoff.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Tier-3-Vision-%E2%80%94-gAIa-Artifact-Evolution">Tier 3 Vision — gAIa Artifact Evolution<a class="anchor-link" href="#Tier-3-Vision-%E2%80%94-gAIa-Artifact-Evolution">¶</a></h2><p>The final form of these notebooks is not static HTML — it is a <strong>live
gAIa artifact</strong> where:</p>
<ol>
<li><p><strong>biomeOS routes</strong> every computation through <code>capability.call</code>, so
the notebook is a composition consumer, not an implementation.</p>
</li>
<li><p><strong>Provenance trio wraps</strong> every cell execution: <code>session.create</code> before
the cell, <code>event.append</code> for each intermediate result, <code>session.commit</code>
after the cell, <code>braid.create</code> to link the notebook run into the
global provenance graph.</p>
</li>
<li><p><strong>petalTongue renders</strong> visualizations server-side using its grammar
of graphics engine (manim-style), replacing matplotlib with
<code>GrammarExpr</code> specifications that are resolution-independent.</p>
</li>
<li><p><strong>Click any data point</strong> and the provenance chain lets you trace back
to the source paper, the external API call (with BLAKE3 hash), the
Rust computation, and the primal composition that produced it.</p>
</li>
<li><p><strong>Reproduction envelope</strong> — the provenance metadata embeds enough
context to recreate the entire computation environment locally via
plasmidBin, allowing anyone to fork, modify, and contribute back
through ionic contracts.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>This is the path from static notebook to living gAIa commons artifact.
wetSpring's Tier 1 (frozen) and Tier 2 (live IPC) are stepping stones
on this evolution.</p>
<hr/>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/ecoPrimals/wetSpring">ecoPrimals/wetSpring</a></p>
</div>
